prompt:
TASK: You are reviewing the design of a backtest 'simulator' page for this trader.
1. From your knowledge of established tools (TradingView Strategy Tester, MetaTrader 5 Strategy Tester visual mode, NinjaTrader Strategy Analyzer, QuantConnect, Backtrader/backtesting.py plots, FX Replay / TradingView Bar Replay), list what each shows to let a trader check a strategy: views, markers, panes, interactions. Be concrete; say which are standard and which are rare.
2. Explain in plain words (for the trader) the basic idea of running a simulation: the rule is checked on every candle, trades happen only where it fires, and how standard tools show that (all trades marked on one continuous chart vs one trade at a time).
3. Propose the minimum set of visuals this page needs, in priority order, each with: what it shows, why the trader needs it, which established tool does the same, and size S/M/L. Respect: no prices (percent from entry or from a reference only), static HTML page, one test at a time.
4. Critique the in-progress per-trade candle panel: keep, change, or replace, and why. Note anything confusing for a non-developer.
5. List the requirements file items you would add or reword.
Answer in Markdown, under 1200 words, plain words, tables where rows are discrete. Do not give trade calls.

OPERATOR (not a developer, a discretionary BTC trader, dictates by voice), latest words: "I need you to refer to what people really do online to check these kind of things, because a clear visual is needed. Even I do not understand how you will show me trades on different phases with all these things, like when you are getting into a trade, when you are getting stopped out. So you can show me only the selected trades, you cannot show me for every candle. I do not understand this idea. So first understand what is the basic idea of running the simulations, with visuals that are really required."

CURRENT PAGE (static HTML, one test at a time): left list of 337 tests with search and filters; right pane per test: title, verdict pill, KPI tiles, 'What was tested' parameters labelled SOURCED/OURS, 'How', then Examples: tables, and a 'replay' = a running-total line of net % per trade with a red dot that steps trade by trade (Play/slider), plus a text line per trade. No candles. Percent distances and timestamps only: prices may not be shown (public repo). Data available: BTCUSDT 1m/5m klines 2022-2025, trades per test with entry time, bars held, net %. A separate local desktop tool (desk.py) has candle charts and settings.
IN PROGRESS: per-trade candle panel for C30 H1 (30m chart): for each of 35 trades, ~45 candles before the signal to 6 after the exit, as % from entry price; markers for signal candle, entry (next open), exit (open after WaveTrend crosses above 0, or 60-candle cap; no stop loss in this rule); WaveTrend pane with -53 and 0 lines; RSI pane with the two divergence lows joined; Prev/Next steps trades and is synced with the running-total dot.
